text: A servant took my horse. <break time="0.8s" /> And another. <break time="0.8s" /> Who walked silently. <break time="0.8s" /> Led me through many dark and winding passages. <break time="0.8s" /> To the room of his master. <break time="0.8s" /> Never had a man changed so terribly. <break time="0.8s" /> In so short a time. <break time="0.8s" /> And I could hardly believe. <break time="0.8s" /> That this pale figure was my old friend. <break time="0.8s" /> His skin was deathly pale. <break time="0.8s" /> And his eyes shone with a strange light. <break time="0.8s" /> His silky hair floating wildly. <break time="0.8s" /> Around his face like a web. <break time="0.8s" /> He suffered from a sickness of the senses. <break time="0.8s" /> So that only the plainest food. <break time="0.8s" /> And the softest clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Were bearable to him. <break time="0.8s" /> The scent of every flower troubled him. <break time="0.8s" /> Even faint light hurt his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> And only a few sounds. <break time="0.8s" /> From stringed instruments. <break time="0.8s" /> Did not fill him with horror. <break time="0.8s" /> I shall perish. <break time="0.8s" /> In this terrible folly. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> For I fear not danger itself. <break time="0.8s" /> But the feeling of terror. <break time="0.8s" /> That it brings. <break time="0.8s" /> He also told me. <break time="0.8s" /> About his beloved sister, the Lady Madeline. <break time="0.8s" /> His only companion for many years. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose long illness had puzzled her doctors. <break time="0.8s" /> While he was speaking. <break time="0.8s" /> She passed slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a distant part of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> And, without having noticed me. <break time="0.8s" /> She disappeared. <break time="0.8s" /> That very evening. <break time="0.8s" /> She gave in to her illness. <break time="0.8s" /> And I learned. <break time="0.8s" /> That I would probably never see her alive again.
